SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SUSTAINABLE SMALL SCALE PRODUCTION OF ENERGY FROM BIOMASS WASTE PRODUCTS.
PROJECT_TITLE: Sustainable small scale production of energy from biomass waste products.
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Developing countries are very dependent on biomass combustion for local energy production. New low cost energy resources, such as rice husk, straw and coconut shell briquettes are needed since wood has become scarce and the price increases continuously. Unfortunately the new energy resources accelerate the problem with high concentrations of particles and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. WHO states that air pollution is the largest single environmental health risk and most severe is the household pollution due to indoor smoke from cooking fuel. The objective of this project is to develop better understanding of how soot particles are formed in biomass combustion, how they burn in the fire and how the resulting ash can be removed from the exhaust. At Gadjah Mada University in Indonesia we will do experimental studies of how briquettes of different design will burn and form soot. At Chalmers University we will focus on how soot particles burn in the fire and can be trapped downstream. The co-workers in Indonesia have experience in briquette manufacturing and small scale biomass combustion. The group at Chalmers has experience in Computational Fluid Dynamics and in removing and burning particles in diesel exhaust. The combined knowledge will lead to new understanding and design concepts that can be used for making new stoves and furnaces with low emissions.

LONG_DESCRIPTION: The project provides support to Indonesia, primarily the Ministry of Energy, in creating and implementing a reliable framework for fostering energy efficiency in the cooling and air-conditioning sector. Since demand for these technologies is rapidly increasing, improving their energy efficiency could make a key contribution to the national climate change mitigation goals.

The funds are dedicated to the Finnish Embassy in Jakarta to enable quality monitoring  as well as to enhance the impact networking and awareness raising related to the Energy and Environment Partnership (EEP).

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT PARTNERSHIP PROGRAM (EEP) IN INDONESIA, BUDGET EXTENSION
PROJECT_TITLE: Energy and Environment Partnership Program (EEP) in Indonesia, budget extension
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Energy and Environment Partnership Program (EEP) aims to increase access to sustainable renewable energy and reduce the growth rate of greenhoue gases in Indonesia. The program promotes wider use of renewable energy and cleaner technology as well as energy efficiency in the rural communities especially among poor and women. The program is especially targeting biomass for energy and is centred in two provinces Riau and Central Kalimantan. The EEP provides co-financing for projects on biomass for energy implemented by community based organisations NGO s and public and private sector. The program also provides support for capasity building in the target areas.
